settings.shortcutRecordDesc: Hold to record (push-to-talk), tap to toggle

settings.launchHint: Start TapWisper when you log in
settings.privacyText: Your data stays on your device.

settings.privacyNoTelemetry: No telemetry or analytics data is collected
settings.privacyDirect: All AI requests go directly to your configured provider
settings.contactDesc: Have a question, found a bug, or want to request a feature? Reach out to us.
settings.apiPrivacyNote: API keys are stored locally on your device and encrypted. They are never sent to any server other than the respective AI provider.
settings.keepMicWarmHint: Starts recording instantly, but keeps the microphone open (mic indicator stays on; Bluetooth headsets switch to call quality).

settings.whisperSharesKey: Whisper uses the same API key as Together AI.
settings.speechLanguagesHint: Pick the languages you dictate in. Auto-detect works for most people; choosing helps short phrases come out in the right language.
settings.keepRecordingsHint: Lets you replay a dictation or transcribe it again from History. Audio never leaves this device, and only the last 50 are kept.
settings.dictionaryMoved: Names, brands and jargon you want recognized now live in your Dictionary, along with the misspellings to fix.
settings.privacyAudioKept: Audio of your last 50 dictations stays on this device for replay
settings.dictationTranslateHint: Speak in any language; TapWisper pastes the translation.
settings.notetakerPermissionMac: To hear the other participants, TapWisper needs Screen & System Audio Recording (System Settings → Privacy & Security). Only audio is used — nothing on your screen is recorded.
settings.notetakerPermissionLinux: Linux can’t capture app audio directly. TapWisper uses a “Monitor of …” input (PulseAudio / PipeWire) when one is available; otherwise only your microphone is recorded.
settings.notetakerPermissionWin: The meeting’s audio is captured from your speakers or headset output — no extra permission is needed.
settings.notetakerPrivacyAudio: Audio is sent to your voice provider for transcription and is not stored
settings.notetakerPrivacyLocal: Transcripts, notes and summaries stay on this device
settings.notetakerPrivacyConsent: Always let people know when you’re taking notes
settings.notetakerHint: Meeting notes from your microphone and the call’s audio — no bot joins the meeting.
settings.recognizeMeetingsHint: When a Zoom, Meet, Teams or Slack call starts, offer to take notes.
settings.captureMeetingAudioHint: Hear the other participants, not just you. Turn off for in-person meetings.
settings.autoSummarizeHint: Write a summary with decisions and next steps when you stop.
settings.meetingTranslateHint: Shows a live translation under each line. Uses your AI provider.

onboarding.microphoneDesc: Required for voice dictation and audio recording. TapWisper uses your microphone to transcribe speech into text.
onboarding.accessibilityDesc: Required for global keyboard shortcuts and inserting text into other applications via simulated keystrokes.
onboarding.screenRecordingDesc: Required for reading selected text from other applications so TapWisper can process it with AI.
onboarding.welcomeBody: Hold a key, talk naturally, let go — your words appear in whatever app you are typing in. Mixed languages included.
onboarding.welcomeSample: Sounds great — let’s meet Thursday at 4 and go over the launch plan.
onboarding.permissionsBody: TapWisper listens only while you hold your key, and types into the app you are using. Your system asks you to confirm that once.
onboarding.micBody: Built-in and wired microphones are the most accurate. Say a few words and watch the bars.
onboarding.micQuestion: Do the bars move when you speak?
onboarding.shortcutBody: Hold it while you talk and let go to insert the text. Tap it once to keep listening hands-free.
onboarding.shortcutTest: Hold it and speak — does the key light up?
onboarding.shortcutWorks: It works. You’re ready to dictate.
onboarding.shortcutAccessibilityHint: Nothing happens? TapWisper needs Accessibility access to hear the key.
onboarding.languagesBody: Pick the languages you dictate in, or leave it on auto-detect. You can change this any time in Settings.
onboarding.doneBody: Click into any text field, hold your key and speak. Everything you dictate is kept in your history on this device.

triggerModal.delayHint: Optional delay before executing the shortcut
triggerModal.exactExplanation: Say only this phrase, e.g. just “open spotify”. The trigger fires only when your whole utterance is the phrase, so it never runs in the middle of normal dictation.
triggerModal.keyboardShortcutHint: Enter the shortcut to simulate (e.g. Cmd+K, Ctrl+Shift+P)
triggerModal.modeBackgroundDesc: Runs silently without opening any windows
triggerModal.modeVisualDesc: Shows commands in your terminal app
triggerModal.noShortcuts: No shortcuts found. Make sure you have shortcuts in the Shortcuts app.
triggerModal.phraseHint: The phrase that activates this trigger when spoken
triggerModal.phrasePlaceholder: e.g. google, ask ai, open spotify
triggerModal.prefixExplanation: Start with the trigger phrase, then say your input. Everything after the phrase is passed to the action. Multi-word phrases also work mid-sentence.
triggerModal.quickPresets: Quick Presets (click to add as “Before” text)
triggerModal.responseClipboardDesc: Copy response to clipboard for manual pasting
triggerModal.responseHandlingHint: How should the AI response be delivered?
triggerModal.responseInjectDesc: Insert AI response directly at cursor position
triggerModal.responseModalDesc: Display result in the floating panel
triggerModal.searchQueryHint: Build your search query by adding text before or after what you say
triggerModal.showOutputDesc: Show the command output in the floating panel when it finishes
triggerModal.stepActionType: Choose what action this trigger performs
triggerModal.stepConfigure: Configure the action and set your trigger phrase
triggerModal.stepPhrase: Set the phrase that activates this trigger
triggerModal.systemPromptPlaceholder: You are a helpful AI assistant...
triggerModal.webSearchHow: Say the trigger phrase followed by your search query. For example, say “Google best coffee shops” to search for “best coffee shops”.
triggerModal.windowHow: Saying the trigger phrase moves the frontmost window to the layout you pick below. For example, a “window left” trigger for the left half and a “window full” trigger for fullscreen.
triggerModal.windowManagementHint: Select which layout this trigger will apply

mic.unavailable: Audio input is not available here.
mic.bluetoothWarning: Bluetooth headsets switch to low-quality call audio while the mic is on, which hurts accuracy. Prefer your built-in or a wired microphone.

speechLanguages.summaryAuto: Auto-detect: the language is recognized each time you speak.
speechLanguages.summaryMixed: Mixed: you can switch between {{languages}} mid-sentence.
speechLanguages.mixBody: Select every language you speak. With two or more selected, TapWisper keeps each word in the language you said it in — nothing gets translated.

dictionary.title: Dictionary
dictionary.subtitle: Names, brands and jargon TapWisper should always get right. Words here are favored during recognition, and anything listed as “often misheard as” is corrected to the right spelling.
dictionary.duplicate: This word is already in your dictionary.
dictionary.termRequired: Enter a word or name first.
dictionary.emptyBody: Add the words that come out wrong — your name, your company, product names, technical terms.
dictionary.deleteMessage: “{{term}}” and its corrections will be removed.

style.title: Style
style.subtitle: Decide how your dictation should read in each kind of app — buttoned-up for email, relaxed for chats.
style.smartFormattingBody: Uses your AI provider to tidy every dictation: removes filler words, applies your corrections (“at four — no, five”), turns spoken lists into lists and fixes punctuation. It never translates.
style.noKey: Smart Formatting needs an API key for {{provider}}. Until then, dictation is pasted exactly as transcribed.
style.disabledHint: Turn on Smart Formatting to apply these styles.

meetings.title: Meetings
meetings.subtitle: Notes, transcripts and summaries of your calls — recorded on this computer, no bot in the meeting.
meetings.emptyBody: Start notes when a call begins. TapWisper listens to you and to the meeting, writes a live transcript, and summarizes it when you stop.
meetings.notFound: This meeting is no longer available.
meetings.deleteMessage: Its transcript, notes and summary will be removed from this device.
meetings.askHint: e.g. “What did we decide about pricing?”
meetings.speakersHint: “Others” is everyone on the call’s audio.

notepad.audioDenied: Only your microphone is recorded. To hear the others, allow TapWisper in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Screen & System Audio Recording, then start again.
notepad.audioUnavailable: Microphone only: this computer can’t capture meeting audio. Works for in-person meetings or calls on speakers.
notepad.audioOff: Meeting audio is off in Settings, so only your microphone is recorded.
notepad.readyMeetingPermission: Asks for permission on first use
notepad.readyMeetingMonitor: Uses a “Monitor of …” input if available
notepad.startBody: Records your microphone and the meeting’s audio on this computer — no bot joins the call. You get a live transcript and a summary when you stop.
notepad.readyMicDenied: Blocked — allow it in system settings
notepad.noRecent: Your meetings will show up here.
notepad.summaryLive: Your summary is written when you stop recording.
notepad.summaryInterrupted: The recording was interrupted. You can still summarize what was captured.
notepad.summaryShort: This meeting was short, so no summary was written automatically.
notepad.notesPlaceholder: Jot down what matters — decisions, names, follow-ups. Your notes shape the summary.
notepad.transcriptListeningHint: Lines appear here every few seconds as people speak.
notepad.errorEmpty: Nothing was said yet, so there is nothing to work with.
notepad.errorNoKey: Add an API key for your AI provider in Settings → AI Provider first.
notepad.errorMicDenied: TapWisper can’t use the microphone. Allow it in your system privacy settings.
notepad.errorMicNotFound: No microphone found. Connect one and try again.
notepad.errorMicInUse: The microphone is busy in another app.
notepad.errorNoVoiceKey: Add an API key for your voice provider in Settings → AI Provider to transcribe meetings.
notepad.errorTranscription: Part of the audio couldn’t be transcribed. Recording continues.
